Full crash report: https://gitlab.com/justinmk/gist/snippets/1840201

@bfredl mentions in https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/7081#issuecomment-323520191 :

>  `rpcstop()` is _strongly_ deprecated with the channels PR. 

Does that mean the solution is to simply remove `rpcstop()` from `remote/host.vim` ?

Had some time to debug this. Seems to be the same case as https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/7081 . Analysis follows:

    remote/host: python3 host registered plugins []nvim: ../src/nvim/event/wstream.c:78:
      _Bool wstream_write(Stream *, WBuffer *): Assertion `!stream->closed' failed.
    Aborted (core dumped)

- af993da4351d (`receive_msgpack`) tried to hack around similar/same issue.
- Hack was removed in 5215e3205a07.

Order of events concerning channel 163 (see logs below):

  1. Channel's in-stream (0x2ba86c0) is **closed** by `f_rpcstop`..`process_stop`.
  2. `receive_msgpack` parses the channel out-stream (0x2ba8860)
  3. Invokes "nvim_command_output" API method.
  4. Writes result to the **closed** in-stream  => **abort**

> Does that mean the solution is to simply remove rpcstop() from remote/host.vim ?

We should do this anyway, but I doubt it will fix the crash. The reason `rpcstop()` is deprecated is because it treats sockets and jobs differently in a way that doesn't make sense. It should still do the documented thing when it is called (which is equivalent to one of `jobstop` or `chanclose` by literally calling the implementation of those).

> Does that mean the solution is to simply remove rpcstop() from remote/host.vim ?

Using `chanclose()` seems to avoid the issue. Whereas `jobstop()` triggers `process_stop`..`stream_may_close` which again closes the in-stream.

The assert in `wstream_write` seems like a contradiction: events have no guaranteed order. Should we remove the assert? Or, should `process_stop` try to flush the channel before closing its streams?

There seems to be nothing weird with the assertion, you cannot write to a closed stream. The problem could  be that `channel->rpc.closed` is not set early enough (maybe it can be set from the same event that marks the wstream as closed), which would safely abort the write.
i e `f_jobstop` probably needs to invoke `rpc_close` directly or indirectly, before calling `process_stop`.
@bfredl That seems to work. I will send a PR. Thanks!
